messages.subject: Re: question for coloring
parts:
hi, Hadley (also CC to the mailist)

I've searched the scale_fill_discrete function, but I can not find
where it is in the package. Could you (or others here) please point
out where I can find helps for this function?

BTW, I am not sure if I explained my problem clearly. Actually, what
I want to implement is, I have hist_cut + geom_bar(position="dodge")
to draw multiple histograms side-by-side on one figure (as the example
in http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_histogram.html). My question is: how
can I use my own color on the filling for each histogram, either in
geom_bar() or in geom_density().

Thanks for anyone who would like help me.

Xianjun


---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hi Xianjun,

You want scale_fill_discrete since you're manipulating the fill
aesthetic. And generally it's a better idea to send requests for help
to the ggplot2 mailing list as except in very simple cases (like this
one) you're likely to receive a faster response there.

Hadley

> > (http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_histogram.html). They are quite helpful.
> >
> > My question is: how can I change the colors (e.g. the density curve) myself?

> > Here is code I tried for that. But it does not work.
> >
> > cols<=c("type1"="black","type2" = "lightgray","type3"="red","type4" =
> > "gray","type5" = "blue")
> > ggplot(dat, aes(x=values,groups=types,fill=cols,colour=cols))+
> > geom_density(fill=cols, alpha=0.5)+
> > scale_colour_manual(values = cols)+
> > theme_bw()
> >
> > Could you pls point out what the problem is?
> >
> > Thanks
> >
> > Xianjun
> >

messages.author: f4bfc22ad77d6303
messages.subject: Re: question for coloring
parts:
hi, Hadley

Sorry to bother you again. I am really learning a lot about ggplots
these days.

But I still have my question here: how to set customised colors for
both histogram filling and density line?

For example,

x <- data.frame(X=rnorm(1000, mean=0))
y <- data.frame(Y=rnorm(1000, mean=3))
xy <- cbind(x, y)
g <- ggplot(xy)
g +
geom_histogram(aes(x=X, fill = "A"), colour=alpha("red", .2),
binwidth = 0.5)+
geom_histogram(aes(x=Y, fill = "B"), colour=alpha("blue", .2),
binwidth = 0.5)+
scale_fill_manual("Case", c("A" = alpha("red", 0.5), "B"=alpha
("blue",0.5)))

or

g +
geom_density(aes(x=X, fill = "A"), fill=NA, colour="red")+
geom_density(aes(x=Y, fill = "B"), fill=NA, colour="blue")+
scale_fill_manual("Case", c("A" = alpha("red", 0.5), "B"=alpha
("blue",0.5)))

works well for the user-defined color, but if I want them displayed
together in one figure:
g +
geom_histogram(aes(x=X, fill = "A"), colour=alpha("red", .2),
binwidth = 0.5)+
geom_histogram(aes(x=Y, fill = "B"), colour=alpha("blue", .2),
binwidth = 0.5)+
geom_density(aes(x=X, fill = "A"), fill=NA, colour="red")+
geom_density(aes(x=Y, fill = "B"), fill=NA, colour="blue")+
scale_fill_manual("Case", c("A" = alpha("red", 0.5), "B"=alpha
("blue",0.5)))

This won't work. The density lines seem hidden somewhere. What's
wrong with the code?

BTW, I also tried another way:

col=c('gray','red')
x <- data.frame(value=rnorm(5000, mean=0), case="A")
y <- data.frame(value=rnorm(5000, mean=3), case="B")
xy <- rbind(x, y)
ggplot(xy, aes(x=value, fill=case, group=case)) +
stat_bin(alpha=0.5, binwidth=0.1, position="dodge",aes(y=..density..))
+
geom_density(fill=NA, colour=col)+
scale_fill_manual(values = col)

It's closer to what I wanted, but still, the line colors of density
are gray, instead of the colors I set. It seems colour=col in
geom_density() does not work.

Could you please point out where I should make a change?

Regards,

Xianjun

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: question for coloring
parts:
Hi,

On Sun, Dec 6, 2009 at 9:38 PM, Xianjun <ster...@gmail.com> wrote:
[snip]

>
> This won't work. The density lines seem hidden somewhere.  What's
> wrong with the code?

The first plot (histogram) has a y scale that extend to about 150,
while the second one (density) goes to about 0.3, so I guess the
reason you don't see the lines is because they are squashed against
the x axis. You probably want to scale either the histogram or the
density.

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: question for coloring
parts:
Hi Xianjun,

Position adjustments, like dodging, only work within a layer, not
between layers. You'll need to reshape your data to long format and
use something like fill = treatment to get it to work.

Hadley
